THE HEADLINES:

  1. Reduced prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs to come into effect from Monday; 76 pharmaceutical companies report revised MRP for over one thousand and two hundred anti-cancer formulations.
  2. Home Minister Amit Shah holds high level review meeting on key issues of national security including narcotics control, cybercrime and border security.
  3. Celebration begins for Diwali all over the country; President and Prime Minister extend greetings on the eve of festival of lights; Vice President attends Deepotsav celebrations in Ayodhya.
  4. Railways make elaborate arrangments in view of festive season; Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw monitors operational efficiency and passenger management at Rail Bhawan.
  5. In Yemen, 25 people killed and 30 injured in airstrikes in Taiz province.
  6. In Men’s cricket, India beat New Zealand by four runs at Wellington taking lead of 2-Nil in a five-match series.

<><><> 

The Government has said that the revised prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs will come into effect from Monday. Recently, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority had capped trade margins on Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of these anti-cancer drugs. We have a Report :-

“The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers informed that as on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for one thousand and two hundred twenty five anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs.It added that the reduction in the MRP have been reported in over one thousand formulations of anti-cancer medicines with 600 brands reporting above 50 per cent reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45 per cent. The Ministry said that as a result of the price reductions the estimated annual savings to consumers would be more than three thousand five hundred crore rupees. It also said that every retailer, dealer, hospital and institution is required to prominently display revised MRP list of anti-cancer medicines on their websites and in their premises. With Anand, Samarth Singh, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

<><><> 

Union Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a high-level review meeting in Ahmedabad today and held extensive discussions on multiple facets of state and national security. He reviewed progress on key issues including border and coastal security, narcotics control, cybercrime, and disaster management. Topics like the Citizenship Amendment Act, the upcoming census, and the Agniveer scheme were also discussed. Mr Shah also assessed the law and order and citizen security situation in Gujarat ahead of Diwali. It was attended by Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Minister of State for Home Harsh Sanghavi, and senior officials from the Union Home Ministry, the State Home Department, and various security agencies.

Stressing the urgency of tackling the drug menace, the Union Home Minister urged officials to work towards achieving the goal of a ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’ by 2029.

<><><> 

Celebration has begun for festival of lights, Diwali. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have extended greetings to all Indians living in India and abroad on the eve of the festival. In a message, the President said that the festival of Diwali marks the victory of virtues over negative tendencies. She added that the festival also signifies the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. She said that on this occasion, people worship Lord Ganesh for auspicious beginnings and well-being, and Goddess Mahalakshmi for prosperity. President Murmu also wished for good health, happiness and prosperity of every citizen of the country. She also urged everyone to preserve the environment and live with harmony. The President also appealed to the youth to contribute in building a Viksit Bharat.

Sharing a video message on social media, the Prime Minister said that the festival of lights illuminates the entire country and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. Mr Modi wished that the festival and the times ahead bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone.

Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Vice President C P Radhakrishnan at the Uprashtrapati Bhawan in New Delhi and exchanged Deepawali greetings.

<><><>

Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan today attended the grand tenth Deepotsav celebrations in Ayodhya. The annual event is organised every year on the occasion of Chhoti Diwali since Yogi Adityanath became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017. More than 30 Lakh earthen lamps illuminated on the 56 ghats of the sacred Saryu River this evening. Our correspondent reports that Governor Anandiben Patel, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and devotees from India and abroad were present on the occasion.

“Appreciating Ayodhya’s spiritual heritage and modern development, the Vice President said that the holy city is rapidly transforming into a grand spiritual destination while preserving its divine legacy. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath performed the Saryu Aarti and while addressing the gathering, he said that Lord Shri Ram represents India’s self-respect and that is why Ayodhya has been recognised in the scriptures as the foremost among the seven sacred cities, known as Sapta Puri. A spectacular laser show, along with live cultural performances, was organised at Ram Ki Paidi. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex was also illuminated with one lakh earthen lamps. Sushil Chandra Tiwari, Akashvani News, Lucknow.”

<><><> 

The festival of lights, Diwali, will be celebrated with traditional fervor and gaiety across Gujarat tomorrow. Details from our correspondent:

“In major cities including Ahmedabad, Surat, Rajkot, and Vadodara, people are crowding the markets to buy clay lamps, rangoli colours, traditional sweets, and new clothes.  Homes and office buildings have been brightly decorated with colourful lights . Tomorrow evening, families will pray to Goddess Lakshmi to ask for good health and wealth. Meanwhile, the state government and local officials have asked citizens to follow safety rules and choose eco-friendly celebrations.  Karan Samrat,Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.”

<><><> 

In view of Diwali festival, several arrangements have been made in the National Capital to ensure a safe and secure festival. The Delhi Fire Services has drawn up an extensive emergency response plan to deal with fire incidents during the festival.

Talking to Akashvani News, Chief Public Relations Officer at Delhi Fire Service Abhilash Kumar Malik said that as part of the preparations, 71 fire stations, 50 Quick Response Vehicles and 20 Motorcycle First Responder units will be deployed on Diwali to tackle fire related incidents.

Major hospitals in Delhi are fully prepared to deal with the cases of burn injuries during Diwali.

 <><><>

Ahead of the Diwali celebrations, wishes have begun pouring in from world leaders and diplomats across the globe, including those serving in India. UAE Vice President Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum in a post on X, extended his Diwali greetings to people celebrating the festival in the United Arab Emirates and around the world.

European Union Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recalled his first Diwali experience in the country. He described it as a beautiful experience, with lights illuminating every corner.

<><><>

Bringing festive cheer to Dalal Street, both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will host the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session tomorrow. According to the circular released by the exchanges, the markets will operate between 2:20 and 3:30 in the afternoon.

The session also marks the beginning of new Hindu financial year, Vikram Samvat 2083, which starts on Diwali.

<><><> 

Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw today reviewed the functioning of War Room providing live visual feeds from railway stations, covering critical areas such as platforms, foot-over bridges and station surroundings. He reviewd the arrangments at Rail Bhawan in New Delhi amid the ongoing festive season.

“During the review meeting, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw   highlighted  the role of technology in strengthening real-time monitoring, operational efficiency and passenger management. Talking to media, Mr Vaishnaw said that  Indian Railways has significantly strengthened its festive-season arrangements through improved crowd management, special train services and dedicated passenger holding areas at around 20 stations including New Delhi and Anand Vihar Terminal.He informed that over 18 thousand  special trains are being operated during the festivals of Diwali and Chhath Puja as compared to around 12 thousand last year.

The arrangements at Stations  also include dedicated ticket counters and multiple scanning facilities to ensure smooth passenger movement. Besides 700 AI cameras have also been installed to strengthen surveillance and security at stations. Anand Kumar, Akashvani News ,Delhi .”

<><><> 

President Droupadi Murmu today extended greetings on the completion of 151 years since the composition of the national song, Vande Mataram. In a social media post, she underscored that during the freedom movement, Vande Mataram served as a rallying cry of courage, unity and resolve for patriots. The President emphasised that even today, Vande Mataram continues to symbolise national identity, self-respect and devotion to the motherland.

<><><> 

In Yemen, 25 people were killed and 30 others injured after airstrikes hit a market in southwestern Taiz province of the country today. Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson Anees Alsabahi confirmed the casualties in a post on X, saying the strikes targeted a market in the al-Waziyah district. The Saudi-backed Yemeni military and Houthi rebels have traded accusations over responsibility for the deadly attack.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s Information Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The latest attack comes amid renewed hostilities in Yemen. Taiz province is largely under Houthi control, while the rebels have maintained a siege around the provincial capital, where the Saudi-backed government and its forces are based.

<><><> 

In ODI Men’s Cricket, India defeated New Zealand by four runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method following a rain stoppage at the Hnry Stadium in Wellington today. India were 113 for seven in 26 overs, and needed 22 runs from 66 balls when play was called off.

Batting first, New Zealand were bowled out for 134 following a disastrous outing in rainy Wellington. India won the first ODI of the five-match series by five wickets, and now leads the rubber 2-nil.                                                                                

 <><><>

  2. Home Minister Amit Shah holds high level review meeting on key issues of national security including narcotics control, cybercrime and border security.
  3. Celebration begins for Diwali all over the country; President and Prime Minister extend greetings on the eve of festival of lights; Vice President attends Deepotsav celebrations in Ayodhya.
  4. Railways make elaborate arrangments in view of festive season; Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw monitors operational efficiency and passenger management at Rail Bhawan.
  5. In Yemen, 25 people killed and 30 injured in airstrikes in Taiz province.
  6. In Men’s cricket, India beat New Zealand by four runs at Wellington taking lead of 2-Nil in a five-match series.

THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Election Commission provides fresh chance to voters left out of draft electoral rolls in seven states, including Delhi and Maharashtra.
  2. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw launches the Semicon India 2.0 web application portal to strengthen the country’s semiconductor and electronics ecosystem.
  3. Stage 3 of GRAP comes into force across Delhi-NCR enforcing tighter curbs as air quality worsens.
  4. Railways operating around 18,000 special trains during the festive season.
  5. Stock market surges by over two per cent; Rupee also gets stronger against the US dollar.
  6. In Men’s cricket, the second ODI of five-match series between India and New Zealand to be played in Wellington tomorrow morning.

 

<><><> 

 

The Election Commission today directed Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to provide one more opportunity to voters who were left out during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). In a statement, the Commission said that voters who were issued enumeration forms but whose names could not be included in the draft electoral roll on account of being marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate will be provided one more opportunity to get their names included in the final electoral roll. More from our correspondent:

 

“The Commission has directed Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to display the lists of such electors afresh and facilitate the submission of their Enumeration Forms. The booth Level Officers have also been asked to contact the electors and assist them with the process, including online submission through the ECINET platform. Special provisions have also been made for electors who have shifted residence within the state and homeless persons. The Commission has also asked to establish a monitoring mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector is deprived of the opportunity in the Final Electoral Roll, while preventing duplicate enrolments. With Anupam, Suparna Saikia, Akashwani News, Delhi.”

 

<><><>                      

 

Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today launched the Semicon India 2.0 web application portal in New Delhi. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Vaishnaw said the transformation of country’s electronics industry over the past ten years reflects the success of collective efforts by the government and industry. He said the progress made so far is only the beginning and is the foundation for the growth of the electronics industry and Atmanirbhar Bharat. He said that the country is progressively moving deeper into the electronics value chain through various programmes and approvals.

 

<><><> 

 

The Centre has directed all traders, wholesalers, Big Chain Retailers and processors across all States and Union Territories to declare their stock positions of rice and paddy. Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Ministry said that all entities stocking rice and paddy are required to disclose their stock positions every Friday on the Food Stock Portal and ensure that the information furnished is accurate and regularly updated.

 

The Ministry said, the government is closely monitoring food grain prices, particularly rice, and undertaking a series of policy interventions to ensure adequate domestic supplies, maintain price stability, prevent hoarding and safeguard consumer interests.

 

The Central government has also doubled the target quantity of rice for sale through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme for 2026-27. It has been increased from 25 lakh metric tonnes to 50 lakh metric tonnes.

 

<><><> 

 

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said the country has been freed from Naxalism under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the police of several states, along with paramilitary forces brought an end to this five-decade-old menace. Mr. Shah said this while presenting the President’s Colour to the Uttarakhand Police in Dehradun today.

 

The Home Minister pointed out that another serious problem, the menace of drugs confronts the nation. He said making India drug-free is country’s resolve and the government has decided that by the end of 2029, India will be completely drug-free, and those engaged in the drug trade will be put behind bars.

 

During the President’s Colour investiture ceremony, Mr. Shah congratulated the Uttarakhand Police on receiving the President’s Colour and said that Uttarakhand Police has become the 16th force in the country to receive this highest honour.

<><><> 

 

The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas today invoked Stage-3 of Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across the entire Delhi – NCR. The decision came after Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded 380 today, placing it in the Very Poor category. This is in addition to the existing actions under Stages 1 and 2 of the GRAP. The Sub-Committee on GRAP today held meeting in New Delhi and reviewed the air quality scenario in the region.

 

The restrictions include a complete ban on all construction and demolition activities including earthwork, trenching, and Road construction activities and major repairs.

 

<><><> 

 

The Supreme Court today termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR, and said immediate, medium and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index. Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also expressed concern over bumper-to-bumper traffic in Delhi-NCR.

The bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood. On stubble burning, the bench stressed the need to educate farmers about using machines instead of resorting to farm fires.     

 

<><><> 

 

The Supreme Court today reaffirmed its 11th March verdict which had held that the salary or income of a parent employed in a PSU or the private sector could not by itself be treated as the determinative criterion for creamy-layer exclusion for the Other Backward Classes. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and R Mahadevan also rejected the Centre’s plea to make the verdict applicable only prospectively.

 

On 11th March, the top court had given the government six months to implement the judgment which was extended by two months today. The apex court said the government remains at liberty to formulate its policy concerning reservation and the creamy layer criteria, in accordance with the Constitution and the principles laid down by the court.

 

<><><> 

 

Railways is operating around 18 thousand special trains in view of the festive season, including Diwali and Chhath. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said this after inspecting the holding areas of New Delhi Railway Station this evening.

 

Mr Vaishnaw also informed that more than 700 AI-enabled cameras have been installed at New Delhi Railway Station to monitor passenger movement and ensure effective crowd management.

 

<><><> 

 

Dhanteras is being celebrated today. This festival marks the beginning of a series of celebrations of Narak Chaturdashi, also known as Choti Diwali or Kali Chaudas, the main Diwali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.

 

On this day, devotees worship Lord Dhanvantari, Goddess Lakshmi, and Lord Kuber. This day is deemed auspicious for making new purchases, especially gold or silver articles and new utensils. In Delhi, a large number of people were seen shopping for Dhanteras across major markets of the national capital, including Chandni Chowk, Chawri Bazaar, Lajpat Nagar, Sarojini Nagar, Laxmi Nagar, Sadar Bazaar, Connaught Place, and Karol Bagh.

 

<><><> 

 

The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the date sheet for Class 10th and 12th board examinations 2027. The examinations for both classes will begin on 16th of February next year. According to the official timetable, Class 10 exams will conclude on 9th March and Class 12 exams will continue till 9th April.

 

<><><> 

 

The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also likely to prevail over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal till Monday. 

 

<><><> 

 

Benchmark domestic equity indices Sensex and Nifty surged over two per cent today, extending their stellar run for the seventh straight session. The rupee also got stronger against the US Dollar. A report:-

 

“Defying weak global cues, the Sensex jumped one thousand 718 points to close at 81 thousand 28. The Nifty climbed 494 points to settle at 25 thousand 30. The broader market on the National Stock Exchange underperformed the frontline indices. The Midcap 100 index ended almost flat with a negative bias, while the Smallcap 100 index dropped over 0.8 per cent. Meanwhile, in the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 56 paise to close at 93 rupees and 91 paise against the US dollar. WITH AYUSHI’s Report, ARJUN CHAUDHURI FOR AKASHVANI News.”

 

<><><> 

 

Credit extended by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) registered a year-on-year growth of 15.4 per cent in September 2026, up from 13.3 per cent in the same month last year. According to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India today, retail loans recorded the strongest growth, accelerating to 21.9 per cent in September compared to 16.8 per cent a year ago. Within the retail segment, housing loans, loans against gold jewellery and vehicle loans witnessed faster growth. Credit to agriculture and allied activities also registered a sharp improvement.

 

<><><> 

 

In Men’s Cricket, second ODI of the five-match series between India and New Zealand will be played in Wellington tomorrow morning. The match will begin at 7:30 AM Indian Standard Time. The visitors will look to extend their lead to 2-0, after registering a five-wicket victory in the rain-affected opening match in Auckland. New Zealand, on the other hand will aim to bounce back and level the series.

 

New Zealand have suffered a setback as their lead batter Devon Conway is ruled out of the remaining four matches of the series. Left-handed batter Nick Kelly replaces Conway.

 

<><><> 

 

THE HEADLINES ONCE AGAIN:

 

  1. Election Commission provides fresh chance to voters left out of draft electoral rolls in seven states, including Delhi and Maharashtra.
  2. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw launches the Semicon India 2.0 web application portal to strengthen the country’s semiconductor and electronics ecosystem.
  3. Stage 3 of GRAP comes into force across Delhi-NCR enforcing tighter curbs as air quality worsens.
  4. Railways operating around 18,000 special trains during the festive season.
  5. Stock market surges by over two per cent; Rupee also gets stronger against the US dollar.
  6. In Men’s cricket, the second ODI of five-match series between India and New Zealand to be played in Wellington tomorrow morning.

 

<><><>

THE HEADLINES:

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi urges Sports Goods Industry to set new benchmarks in domestic manufacturing; Calls for Made in India sports gear, apparel and footwear for players worldwide.
  2. Centre to set up special committee to re-examine UGC’s 2026 equity regulations to protect interests of all sections of society.
  3. DRDO successfully tests indigenously developed surface-to-surface quasi-ballistic tactical missile Pralay off Odisha coast.
  4. Benchmark domestic indices post strong gains of two and a half per cent; Sensex crosses 79 thousand 300 mark.
  5. In Hockey, India beat Japan 4-1 at Mohali to retain Men’s Asian Champions Trophy.
  6. Portuguese superstar Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from International Football.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called upon India’s sports goods industry to set new benchmarks in domestic manufacturing and strengthen the country’s position in the global market. Mr Modi made these remarks while interacting with the Indian contingent of the recently concluded Asian Para Games in New Delhi this evening. The Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Prime Minister Modi emphasised that sports equipment, apparel and footwear used by players across the world should increasingly be Made in India. 

 

 

The Prime Minister hailed India’s remarkable rise at the Asian Para Games from 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in Japan this year. He said, it reflects the immense talent and potential of the country’s athletes.

 

Speaking at the event, Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya emphasised that athletes and para-athletes are now being accorded equal status, with both receiving equal opportunities, facilities and support.

 

 

India registered its best-ever performance at the Asian Para Games 2026. A total of 97 Indian para-athletes won 114 medals, comprising 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Centre has informed the Supreme Court that it is setting up a special committee to review the the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026. The move comes following concerns that certain provisions within the framework are exclusionary, vague, and susceptible to misuse.

 

 

The UGC notified the 2026 regulations in January this year, replacing the 2012 framework. However, the Supreme Court subsequently stayed the implementation of the new regulations, citing concerns over certain vague provisions and the possibility of their misuse. The court had also restored the 2012 regulations on an interim basis.

 

 

The top court was informed by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta today that the government was examining measures to address students’ concerns and ensure that no section of society feels excluded or threatened. The Apex Court adjourned the batch of petitions for four weeks, observing that the welfare and interests of the younger generation must remain at the centre of the deliberations.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

An Inter-Ministerial Group has recommended asset monetisation proposals involving assets worth more than 1,100 crore rupees for consideration and approval by the Alternative Mechanism. The group is chaired by the Secretary of the Department of Public Enterprises and co-chaired by the Secretary of the Department of Telecommunications. The proposals primarily relate to surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises identified for monetisation.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Central Government has released regular instalment of tax devolution to State Governments amounting to one lakh nine thousand and 19 crore rupees today. The monthly instalment normally released on 10th November has been advanced and released on 5th November in view of the upcoming festive season and to enable States to accelerate capital spending and finance their development and welfare related expenditure.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said, renewable energy sector is helping ensure affordable electricity, reduce industrial costs, generate employment and lower the country’s import bill. Mr Radhakrishnan was addressing the valedictory session of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 in New Delhi today. He noted that India has achieved rapid economic growth while steadily reducing its dependence on fossil fuels.

 

 

 

The summit witnessed the participation of more than 800 international delegates from various countries and the signing of 10 Memorandums of Understanding and framework agreements.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has announced a target of undertaking road projects worth five lakh crore rupees in Uttar Pradesh. He said projects worth one lakh crore rupees have already been completed, another one lakh crore rupees worth of projects are under construction, while projects worth three lakh crore rupees are in the pipeline. Mr Gadkari was addressing a public rally in Jaunpur district after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for various development projects worth around three thousand six hundred and seventy-seven crore rupees. The Minister stressed the need to promote alternative fuels to reduce dependence on imports and enhance farmers’ income.

 

 <><><>

 

 

The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the successfull flight test of the indigenously developed surface-to-surface, short-range tactical quasi-ballistic missile Pralay off the coast of Odisha today. The Defence Ministry said, all the test objectives were fully met as confirmed by the test data captured by various range instruments deployed by Integrated Test Range in Chandipur.

 

 

In a social media post, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the successful trial marks another significant milestone in strengthening India’s indigenous defence capabilities.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Minister and BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri has been elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh. Following the end of the deadline for withdrawal of nominations today, Returning Officer Umesh Kumar Sharma formally declared Mr. Puri elected. The Rajya Sabha seat had fallen vacant following the resignation of Union Minister L. Murugan.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Home Minister and Senior BJP leader Amit Shah today led a foot march in Karnal as part of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’ campaign, also known as ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ at Karnal in Haryana. Addressing the gathering before the march, the senior BJP leader said, Parliament is the highest forum for discussion in a democracy. He alleged that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi neither allows Parliament to function nor participates in parliamentary debates. Mr Shah asserted that the BJP would hold Mr Gandhi accountable at every level, including on the streets, in Parliament and in State Legislative Assemblies. He further said, the ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’ campaign has emerged as an effective platform to respond to the Congress leader.

 

 

 

Later in the day, Mr Shah paid tribute to the martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice in India’s freedom struggle, from the Revolt of 1857 until the country attained independence. Addressing a public meeting in Ambala, the Home Minister said Haryana has made notable contributions to nation-building, from agriculture to sports, apart from its role in the freedom struggle.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri today called on Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu and discussed the wide-ranging engagement and progress in various areas of India-Nepal bilateral cooperation. According to a joint press release issued on the official visit of the Foreign Secretary to Nepal, the two leaders discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Nepalese Prime Minister to India. Mr Misri reached Kathmandu yesterday on a two-day visit to Nepal.

 

 

During the visit, the Foreign Secretary also called on Nepal’s Finance Minister, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, and Minister for Infrastructure Development. More from our correspondent:

 

 

“Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri also interacted with a group of parliamentarians, including members of the India-Nepal Parliamentary Friendship Group and Nepal’s Parliamentary Committee on International Relations and Tourism. During various engagements, the Nepali leadership expressed gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods. Both sides noted with satisfaction the growing engagement in recent times in traditionally strong areas of bilateral cooperation. These include trade and commerce, development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy, and people to people ties as well as newer avenues for collaboration including start-ups, digital connectivity, AI and sports. They reaffirmed their commitment to all round enhancement of the bilateral partnership. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Benchmark domestic equity indices surged around two and a half per cent today, buoyed by positive global cues. We have a report:-

 

 

“The Sensex jumped two thousand nine points, or 2.6 per cent to close at 79 thousand 310. The Nifty climbed 576 points, or 2.4 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 537. Both the indices extended their stellar run for the sixth consecutive session. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index surged nearly 1.9 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index rose almost 0.6 per cent. 

 

 

Meanwhile, in the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 18 paise to close at 94 rupees and 47 paise against the US dollar. With Ayush’s report Anubha Rohatgi for Akashvani News.”

 

 

Meanwhile, global crude oil prices rose today, recovering from steep losses suffered in the previous session.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe till Sunday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh and Odisha tomorrow. Meanwhile, the National Capital will witness mainly clear sky and shallow fog or mist at a few places in the morning hours tomorrow. The air quality in Delhi-NCR continues to remain in the very poor category. Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 374 at 7 PM today.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

In Hockey, India defeated Japan, 4-1 in the final at Mohali today to retain Men’s Asian Champions Trophy for the sixth time. It was a spectacular ‘Chak De India’ moment for the defending champions India. The emphatic victory sparked celebrations across the country, with jubilant fans hailing the triumph as an early Diwali gift to the nation. In the third-place playoff, Malaysia defeated South Korea 5-2 to claim the bronze medal.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

India won a silver medal at the ongoing ISSF World Shooting Championships in Doha today. The trio of Manu Bhaker, Suruchi Singh and Sainyam secured the medal in the women’s 10-metre air pistol team event. China won the gold medal in the event. With this silver medal, India’s overall medal tally has risen to four, comprising one gold and three silver medals.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Portuguese football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, bringing the curtain down on an illustrious career spanning more than two decades. Union Cabinet has also approved two year extension of Agniveers who were earlier set to exit after four years of service. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting in New Delhi today, CDS General NS Raja Subramani said, 75 per cent of Agniveers who had to exit will now be given an additional two-year engagement period, after which the willing Agniveers can enrol in the Armed Forces.

  

 

General Raja Subramani said that under the scheme, the remaining 75 percent of Agniveers will now be offered an additional engagement period of two years. He said, upon the completion of this two-year period, all those Agniveers who are willing to continue will be enrolled into the Armed Forces. He said, the extension will come with higher remuneration.

 

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that the two year extension of Agniveers is aimed at creating a younger, fitter, technologically equipped and future-ready military. In a social media post, Mr Singh said, this will also provide enrollment of all willing Agniveers as regular soldiers after the tenure of 4 or 6 years, who meet the selection criteria.

 

The Union Cabinet has approved 92 Gigawatt-hour energy storage scheme to further strengthen India’s clean energy programme. Briefing media this afternoon in New Delhi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vashnaw said, the scheme will comprise 30 Gigawatt-hour of battery storage, 60 Gigawatt-hour of pumped storage and two Gigawatt-hour for emerging energy storage technologies.

 

The Cabinet has also given nod to the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research, VISTAR Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of over four thousand 371 crore rupees. The VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets.  In a social media post, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the Cabinet has approved the VISTAR) Scheme to transform India’s statistical system.

The Cabinet has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of over two thousand crore rupees over a period of five years. The Prime Minister said that lithium, nickel, and cobalt are essential for EVs, batteries, electronics and defence and India remains heavily dependent on imports of these refined materials.

 

The Cabinet has also approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts, including exclusive POCSO Courts, for a further period of five years from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2031. The Scheme has a total financial outlay of over three thousand 788 crore rupees.

The Iranian government today reiterated that Indian vessels are exempt from restrictions imposed on shipping through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Iranian lawmaker Ahmad Hayat-Moghaddam, Vice Chairman of the Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee said India, China, Iraq and Qatar have been granted exemptions and can navigate the waterway without restrictions.

Meanwhile, senior Iranian political leaders are reportedly urging the country’s military leadership to consider a diplomatic proposal brokered by Qatar, amid growing fears of a renewed military confrontation with the United States.

Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country.

The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing. The Reserve Bank of India has simplified foreign exchange reporting rules for service exporters and importers, easing compliance requirements for individuals and small-value transactions. A report:

 

 

“Under the revised rules, individuals who export services will no longer have to submit a separate Export Declaration Form, or EDF. They will only need to provide the details of the payment received to their authorised bank. This will be treated as submission of the declaration. The same relaxation will apply to other service exporters for payments received up to ten lakh rupees. The RBI has also simplified reporting requirements for imports of services. Banks will now have to report such transactions only when the importer is not an individual resident in India and the invoice or contract value is more than ten lakh rupees. These changes are expected to reduce compliance requirements for small service transactions and make foreign exchange procedures easier. The revised rules were notified on 2nd November and have come into effect retrospectively from 1st October 2026. sweety Jain,akashvani News, MUmbai.”

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has allowed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) to issue depository receipts and list them on GIFT City exchanges, opening up a new avenue for attracting foreign investment. The framework requires approval from at least 75 per cent of unitholders voting in favour of a fresh issue of depository receipts (DRs).

Home Minister Amit Shah has directed that Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) be established in all state capitals by next year. At present, FRRO offices are operational in 20 states. More from our correspondent.

 

 

         

 

“The establishment of these FRRO offices will help foreigners visiting India in obtaining various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. She will now face Germany’s Jolina Reinhold, the reigning Cadet World Champion, in the gold medal match later tonight.
         

 

Meanwhile, Dhinidhi Desinghu has created history by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to qualify for the Youth Olympics final after advancing to women’s 100-metre freestyle medal race.  The 16-year-old from Bengaluru clocked 56.80 seconds to win her heat and finish third overall in the qualifying round.

President Droupadi Murmu has said that every citizen has a responsibility to contribute to social welfare and national development. She called upon people to rise above personal interests and work for the larger good of society and the nation. The President was addressing a function marking the centenary of the sacrifice of Swami Shraddhanand at Gurukul in Haryana’s Kurukshetra, today. She stressed that collective efforts are essential to achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

 

 

Highlighting the life of Swami Shraddhanand, the President said he worked for social harmony and played an important role in India’s freedom struggle.

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

Earlier in the day, President Murmu addressed the Haryana Day celebrations in Kurukshetra, marking the 60th anniversary of the formation of the State. She said, the nationwide Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign has proved to be an important milestone in promoting women’s empowerment. She also said that Haryana had made remarkable progress over the past decade in various aspects of women’s empowerment.

 

Besides Haryana, several other states and Union Territories celebrated their formation day today. These include, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Punjab and Tamil Nadu. The President, Vice President and Prime Minister extended wishes to the people of these states and Union Territories on the occasion.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah today praised the Chandigarh Police for its courage and dedication in combating terrorism and maintaining law and order. He was addressing the 60th Raising Day celebrations of the Chandigarh Police in the city today.The Home Minister said the Chandigarh Police had displayed exceptional courage during the era of terrorism.

On the occasion, Mr Shah conferred the prestigious President’s Police Colour on the force. The honour was approved by President Droupadi Murmu. He also presented the President’s Medals to officers and personnel of the Chandigarh Police.

 

 

 

The Home Minister also flagged off 141 new vehicles for the Chandigarh Police.  Later, Mr Shah inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for several development projects worth 258 crore rupees in Chandigarh.

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit outlined his top priorities to strengthen and modernise the Indian Air force a day after taking charge as the 29th Chief of Air Staff. In his first address today, Indian Air Force Chief coined the guiding theme ‘VAYU’, articulating four distinct pillars that will shape the IAF’s future trajectory. These are Vigilance, Victory and Readiness, self-reliance, Yukti, and Unity of Effort. Through the ‘VAYU’ vision, Air Chief Marshal Dixit articulated a clear direction for an operationally ready, technologically advanced, self-reliant and seamlessly integrated Indian Air Force. He emphasised the need to maintain the highest level of operational preparedness across all formations, with restoring combat strength to sanctioned levels being a top priority.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has hailed the inauguration of the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Train which was flagged off by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that the Vande Bharat Sleeper Train will be a game changer for connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. The Prime Minister added that this train will benefit Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, especially benefitting youngsters, IT professionals and students. The train will cover the journey between the two cities in around 16 hours.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal today intensified into a cyclone named as ‘Murasu, prompting Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up preparedness for another high-intensity storm in less than a week. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the latest storm is very likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm tomorrow morning.  It is likely to cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm between tomorrow midnight to early hours of Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph.

 

The IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh tomorrow. An orange alert has been issued Rayalaseema, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and Telangana tomorrow.

 

Heavy rainfall is also expected over Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Mahe, Odisha and South Interior Karnataka during the next two days.

Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is on high alert, with the state government stepping up precautionary measures to tackle the emerging threat. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm Murasu. It is moving west-northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning. It is expected to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur during the early hours of Wednesday, with wind speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the preparedness and directed departments to coordinate rescue and relief operations. Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams have been deployed. Control rooms have been set up, and evacuation of people from unsafe areas has been ordered. People have been urged to follow official warnings and contact 112 or 1070 for emergencies. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

 

 

Odisha is also preparing for another cyclonic storm, even as thousands of families continue to grapple with the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods. As a precautionary measure, authorities have also opened the gates of the Balimela reservoir. We have a report:

 

 

 

“Southern Odisha, still struggling to recover from the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods, is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall as Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ approaches the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department has forecast rainfall activity in Odisha starting tomorrow, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over southern districts on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput, Nowarangpur and Malkangiri are among the districts requiring close attention, particularly vulnerable hilly areas and flood-prone villages, where fresh rainfall could trigger flash floods and landslides. The state government has identified vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone locations, and initiated the evacuation of people to safer places. District Collectors of vulnerable areas have been kept on high alert. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the National Organ Transplant Games in New Delhi. Addressing the event, the Vice President described the Games as a celebration of the resilience of transplant recipients and demonstrating the life-transforming power of modern medicine.

 

 

 

On the occasion, Mr. Radhakrishnan witnessed an attempt to set a world record, featuring 570 transplant recipients and donors performing Tadasana together. Following the successful attempt, the organisers were presented with a certificate by the World Book of Records, New Delhi, for the ‘Largest Congregation of Transplant Recipients and Donors Performing Tadasana’.

The country’s gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections grew nearly 23 per cent year-on-year to over two lakh 31 thousand crore rupees in October this year. It was driven by robust domestic economic activity and a sharp rise in tax revenue from imports.

<><><> 

 

The Centre has withdrawn the special additional excise duty on petrol exports while increasing export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). Under the revised rates, petrol exports will attract no export duty, compared to the earlier levy of two rupees 50 paise per litre. The export duty on diesel has been increased from eight rupees 50 paise to 11 rupees 50 paise per litre while the levy on ATF has been raised from 10 rupees 50 paise to 11 rupees per litre.

In Badminton, two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has clinched the Women’s Singles title of Hylo Open Super 500 tournament in Germany today, her second title of the season. World No. 8 Sindhu defeated Denmark’s Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14 in the final. Earlier this year, Sindhu made history by winning the Japan Open.

Meanwhile, in the men’s singles final, Lakshya Sen will take on Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie in a short while.

In Archery, India has won four medals at the ongoing Swiss Open IWS Archery Championship in Switzerland. Sachin Chechi, Tania Rani and Priya Gurjar clinched silver medals, while Aditya Wadhwa secured bronze. Sachin won silver in the Compound Under-21 Men’s category after narrowly losing the final to Germany’s Simon Moritz by 145-147. In the Compound Under-21 Women’s category, Tania Rani also claimed silver after losing to Youth World Championship medallist Fenna Stallen in the final. Meanwhile, Priya Gurjar secured another silver medal in the Compound Women’s category. She lost to Mexico’s Andrea Maya Becerra Arizaga . In the Recurve Under-21 Men’s category, Aditya Wadhwa clinched bronze. He defeated Slovenia’s Gal Frank 6-2 in the bronze medal match.

In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand defeated India by seven wickets in the fifth and final T20 International in Hamilton. Despite the loss, India won the five-match series 3-2. The Men in Blue won the first three matches. However, New Zealand made a strong comeback by winning the final two games. They had also defeated India in the fourth T20 International in Auckland on Friday.
